## 6E.1 Convergence of stochastic simulations

SDE simulations are stochastic, so we judge their convergence and stability through statistics of the trajectories, such as mean levels and their standard deviations. Using the [Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process](06c-sde-integrators.qmd) as the test case, design an experiment that measures how the simulation statistics converge as the computational cost grows (take the cost to be proportional to the total simulation length).

## 6E.2 Geometric Brownian motion

Consider a geometric Brownian motion, governed by the SDE

$$ dX = \mu X\,dt + \sigma X\,dW , \tag{1} $$

with positive constants $\mu$ and $\sigma$. Using Euler-Maruyama simulations, show that

**(a)** the mean is $\langle X \rangle = X_0\, e^{\mu t}$, and

**(b)** the variance is $\mathrm{Var}(X) = X_0^2\, e^{2\mu t} \left( e^{\sigma^2 t} - 1 \right)$.

Use $\mu = 0.1$, $\sigma = 0.2$, and $X_0 = 1$.

Hint: simulate many trajectories of the same system with the same parameters and initial condition, differing only in their random draws, then compute the mean and variance at each of several time points. Run at least 100 simulations and evaluate the statistics at 10 time points (choose small $t$ and a short total time to keep the cost down). Check whether the simulated statistics match the formulas above.

## 6E.3 Noise in a flip-flop circuit

Return to the [flip-flop circuit](../03-phase-plane/03h-multi-component.qmd) of Part 3H and add gene-expression noise. Write down the corresponding SDEs, simulate the stochastic dynamics, and describe what kinds of behavior the circuit shows once noise is present.

## 6E.4 Effective potential revisited

We have defined an effective potential for nonlinear systems by analogy with over-damped dynamics ([Part 2D](../02-odes/02d-effective-potential.qmd) and [Part 3G](../03-phase-plane/03g-effective-potential-2d.qmd)), but that definition runs into trouble in higher dimensions. An alternative defines the potential from the occupancy of the phase plane,

$$ U(X, Y) = -\log P(X, Y) , \tag{2} $$

where $P(X, Y)$ is the probability of finding the system near $(X, Y)$. Using the [toggle switch](../03-phase-plane/03a-nullclines.qmd) as an example, run SDE simulations, estimate $P(X, Y)$, and compute this effective potential. Plot the potential along each of the nullclines, and compare it with the over-damped definition.

## 6E.5 Transition state theory

Revisit the transition-rate calculation of [Part 6D](06d-stochastic-transitions.qmd), now varying the noise level. Determine how the transition rate depends on the noise, and check whether the results follow the Arrhenius (Kramers) form for noise-activated barrier crossing [@kramers1940brownian],

$$ \kappa \propto e^{-\frac{\Delta U}{D}} , \tag{3} $$

where $D$ is the noise level and $\Delta U$ the barrier height.

## 6E.6 Deterministic versus stochastic repressilator

The repressilator is a synthetic gene circuit of three genes wired in a repression ring: gene 1 represses gene 2, gene 2 represses gene 3, and gene 3 represses gene 1 [@elowitz2000repressilator]. This cyclic inhibition can drive sustained oscillations in gene expression. We met its deterministic limit cycle in [Part 3H](../03-phase-plane/03h-multi-component.qmd); here we add gene-expression noise and ask how robust the oscillation is.

Writing $x(t)$, $y(t)$, $z(t)$ for the three protein concentrations, the deterministic dynamics are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{dx}{dt} &= \frac{g}{1 + z^n} - x , \\
\frac{dy}{dt} &= \frac{g}{1 + x^n} - y , \\
\frac{dz}{dt} &= \frac{g}{1 + y^n} - z ,
\end{aligned} \tag{4}
$$

where $g$ is the maximal production rate, $n$ the Hill coefficient of repression, and the degradation rate is normalized to 1.

**(a)** Simulate the deterministic system with $g = 50$, $n = 2$, and initial condition $x(0) = 1$, $y(0) = 2$, $z(0) = 3$. Plot $x(t)$, $y(t)$, and $z(t)$ as functions of time.

**(b)** Add a constant noise term to each gene, turning the model into a system of SDEs,

$$
\begin{aligned}
dx &= \left( \frac{g}{1 + z^n} - x \right) dt + \sigma\, dW_x , \\
dy &= \left( \frac{g}{1 + x^n} - y \right) dt + \sigma\, dW_y , \\
dz &= \left( \frac{g}{1 + y^n} - z \right) dt + \sigma\, dW_z ,
\end{aligned} \tag{5}
$$

where $W_x$, $W_y$, $W_z$ are independent Wiener processes and $\sigma$ sets the noise strength. Simulate with the Euler-Maruyama method for $\sigma = 0.05$, $\sigma = 0.5$, and $\sigma = 2.0$, and plot the trajectories in each case.

**(c)** Compare the deterministic and stochastic trajectories. Describe how the amplitude, phase, and period of the oscillations change with the noise level, and comment on whether the oscillation persists or degrades as $\sigma$ increases.

Hint: you will need a multi-variable integrator, a derivative function, and a noise function. The generic multi-variable RK4 routine `RK4_generic` from [Part 3H](../03-phase-plane/03h-multi-component.qmd) handles the deterministic part; for the stochastic part, extend the constant-noise Euler-Maruyama integrator `SDE_Euler_2D` of [Part 6D](06d-stochastic-transitions.qmd) from two variables to three.
